counting_rule:
Counting rule: every scalar +, -, x, / and every elementary function (exp, sqrt, tanh,
sin, cos, min/max) counts as one operation. This undercounts transcendental functions,
which favours the expensive controllers. Feature preprocessing shared by the learned
policies (normalized count, two moving averages and their difference, about 10
operations) is included for them; the other controllers read the same count.

differentiator.basis: low-pass update, difference, scale, offset, depth map

kalman.basis: 3-state predict/update with scalar innovation (about 200 multiplications), control dot product, amplitude normalization, depth map

mlp.basis: 720 MACs, 33 biases, 32 LeakyReLU, tanh, depth map

mlp_large.basis: 5952 MACs, 129 biases, 128 LeakyReLU, tanh, depth map

particle.basis: 512 particles x (328 + 208) rate evaluations x ~107-128 ops, integrator and noise overhead, 164,352 Gaussian variates, likelihood

interpretation: Approximate arithmetic-work estimates, not measured execution time or FPGA latency.
